question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272472/assets/a1015cb8e8c7cd0bcee792c919b5f9c6f0e1ce180e971fcfeda8eecfc8238a47.svg)
Find $P(-4 \leq Y \leq 4).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x, y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $y \geq 0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(4x+y/4)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-(4x+y/4)}]}_{x=0}^{x=\infty } \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(0-{e}^{-(0+y/4)}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-y/4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for $f_Y(y)$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14272472/assets/810669e70e34a95f937272d35174b4ccc72a5a3d6356a322893e516e7b6f4597.svg)

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-4\le Y\le 4) & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-y/4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-{e}^{-y/4}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =(-{e}^{-4/4}+{e}^{0}) \\  & =1-\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$
